facts.statement: The genus Comahuesuchus was described by the paleontologist José Bonaparte in 1991.
facts.quote: It was described by palaeontologist José Bonaparte in 1991.

facts.statement: Comahuesuchus was an extinct notosuchian crocodylomorph that lived in Argentina during the late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Comahuesuchus is an extinct genus of notosuchian crocodylomorphs from the late Cretaceous of Argentina.

facts.statement: A second species, C. bonapartei, was assigned to the genus in 2023 based on fossils from the Sierra Barrosa and Portezuelo Formations.
facts.quote: In 2023 another species, C. bonapartei from the Sierra Barrosa Formation and Portezuelo Formation, was assigned to the genus.

facts.statement: José Bonaparte created the monotypic family Comahuesuchidae within Notosuchia when he described the genus.
facts.quote: para el cual creó la familia monotípica Comahuesuchidae dentro de Notosuchia

facts.statement: The type species C. brachybuccalis was a small animal.
facts.quote: C. brachybuccalis era de tamaño pequeño

facts.statement: Comahuesuchus was distinguished from all other crocodylomorphs by having an extremely short and wide snout.
facts.quote: se diferenciaba de todos los demás crocodiliformes en tener un hocico extremadamente corto y ancho

facts.statement: Its dentition was reduced but included two pairs of canine-like teeth.
facts.quote: con dentición reducida pero con dos pares de caniniformes

facts.statement: The skull morphology makes Comahuesuchus an unusual crocodylomorph.
facts.quote: La morfología del cráneo lo convierte en un cocodriliforme inusual.

facts.statement: Research suggests that Comahuesuchus is more closely related to Mariliasuchus amarali than to other notosuchians.
facts.quote: Comahuesuchus parece, en cambio, estar más cercanamente relacionado con Mariliasuchus amarali

facts.statement: It is debated whether Anatosuchus minor belongs to the Comahuesuchidae family, as some analyses suggest it does not.
facts.quote: el análisis realizado por Martinelli y Andrade et al. (2006) sugiere que A. minor no es un comahuesúquido

facts.statement: Fossils of Comahuesuchus date from the Turonian to Santonian stages, between 93.9 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Santonian (93.9 to 83.6 million years ago)
